title: The Biggest Solar Flare Ever Overwhelmed the Instruments Measuring It

scenes.text: The biggest solar flare ever recorded overwhelmed the satellites measuring it.
It hit on the fourth of November, 2003.
Scientists rate flares by letter: C, M, then X, the strongest class.
This one was rated X28 at best estimate. X-class flares can cause radio blackouts worldwide.
X-ray detectors on several monitoring satellites saturated, so even X28 is a best guess.
The biggest flare ever? Our instruments couldn't see all of it.

description:
The strongest solar flare in recorded history erupted on 4 November 2003 and was rated X28.
It saturated the X-ray detectors on several monitoring satellites, so the rating is a best estimate.
What do you think we'd do if a flare like that hit a bigger target? Comment below.
thumbnail_text: FLARE SO BIG IT BLINDED SATELLITES
first_comment: Our instruments maxed out before the flare did. What's the biggest thing you've ever seen that didn't fit in a measurement?
